title: Honey, Baby, Sweetheart
text:
Honey, Baby, Sweetheart. Deb Caletti. New York: Simon & Schuster Books for Young Readers, 2004. 308p.

Honey, Baby, Sweetheart by Deb Caletti provides young adult readers with the captivating story of sixteen-year-old Ruby McQueen and her ill-fated summer romance. This Caletti's second book proves that she is an author tuned-in to today's youth. Her superb mastery of story elements create tales worth reading.

Ruby, a usually quiet girl, feels a compulsion to take a leap off the edge, like the paragliders she watches at Moon Point just outside her small hometown of Nine Mile Falls, Washington. Ruby jumps onto the back of Travis Becker's motorcycle and begins a downhill summer ride which quickly speeds out of control.

Travis Becker is an aloof rich kid who lives in the gated estate on Cummings Road. When Ruby decides to step through the open gates one day, she encounters Travis and knows there is no going back. "Right away I got that Something About To Happen felling. Right away I knew he was bad, and that it didn't matter." Mesmerized by him, Ruby becomes another person-daring, pretty, clever, enticing. As Travis draws Ruby deeper into his warped rich-boy world, she begins having second thoughts but feels unable to cut the ties that bind her.

Ruby's divorced mother mirrors her relationship dilemma. Still caught in her ex-husband's trap, Ruby's mother can't quite seem to rid herself of this man who continues to impose on her life. Ruby and her younger brother, Chip Jr., become wedged in the cross-fire.

After Ruby sinks to the lowest depths with Travis, she finds help from her librarian mother and a book discussion group of rowdy senior citizens, the Casserole Queens. Ruby decides to help the Queens execute a daring escape for one of their own, Lillian--wrongly imprisoned in a nursing home. It's a mission of the heart to reunite two long-lost lovers before their time expires.

On this humorous and touching escapade, Ruby finally realizes what true love means. "We are all a volume on the shelf of the Nine Mile Falls Library, a story unto ourselves...And love-it is not the book itself, but the binding. It can rip us apart or hold us together."

This story has some of the bittersweet elements of Sharon Creech's Newbery winning Walk Two Moons, combining a troubled girl and quirky seniors on a road-trip. Caletti grounds her characters in everyday-ness but provides the reader with all the insights needed to feel attuned to Ruby's uniqueness. Honey, Baby, Sweetheart is a compelling story sure to please young romance readers.

title: "TRAPS, THE DRUM WONDER"
text:
Terrific book about an exceptional talent! Don't know what the other reviewer is complaining about. I paid full price and don't regret it. (That's about eighteen bucks, with shipping.)
If you like Buddy's kind of music, you'll appreciate the book. In addition: you get plenty of insight into the man, what for me, was an added bonus: Buddy's devotion to friends and good-hearted nature (ie: the passage with Johnny Carson, Count Bassie, et al). Granted, he wasn't always the easiest guy to get along with, but what matters most is that he had a good heart, loved music and those who had the same love and dedication for it as he did. Reading the book made me want to take the albums out and play them, etc.
While I'm at it here, have wanted to express for years now how impressed I was with his daughter Cathy's version of the Sonny Bono tune entitled THE BEAT GOES ON. She does a terririfc cover of it on Buddy's Big Swing Face album recorded years ago. Cathy was only 12 and 1/2, mind you, at the time, and showed great promise in my opinion, and have wondered why she never pursued a singing career, etc.
There is so much more I could say about this book, but it would take too long. You get a good glimpse into what life must have been like for Buddy and his family in this country during the 30's and 40's, etc., (through various interviews with family members), what it was like for him as a gifted kid at age 3 to be traveling the world as "Traps the Drum Wonder," all that.
The only thing that bothered me (and this is a relatively minor objection, if you can even call it that) is the awful photo of Buddy Rich used for the cover, as someone else mentioned as well. I mean, couldn't they have found something more flattering? I think the legendary Buddy Rich deserves better.
All in all: nice job, Mr. Minahan. Thank you.

text:
This book really drives home the first point of survival. Thermal regulation is your first concern (once you are out of an immediately threatening situation). This is importance is noted in the title: 98.6. Keeping your internal body temperature in a very narrow range is important to the proper functioning of not just your muscles and organs, but you mind.

The book goes into extensive details on the ways we lose or gain heat and what to do under a wide range of circumstances to retain or get rid of heat.

As somebody who travels through wide ranges of terrain I appreciated the different climates covered in the book.

Cody uses characters and acronyms to bring humor to a serious situation.
The goal of course is to remember the lessons when a situation presents itself that threatens your ability to maintain the correct body temperature. Some of the acronyms will take awhile to sink in. Definitely something that needs repeated practice.

This is a good book to read and re-read for anybody travelling away from an urban environment.

title: From a dance hall to the outback
text:
Phryne is out dancing at one of her favorite night spots, but the evening was not going particularly well. She was on a job, supervising a particularly annoying young man at the request of his overly possessive mother. Suddenly one of the dancers stumbled to the ground, dead. Unfortunately it was not Phryne's charge who instead of lying quietly on the floor was acting liking a ninny over the event. Phryne once again found herself involved in police affairs as she attempted to sort the various messes the death had caused, including the disappearance of her annoying charge. Oddly enough the answers to some of her questions lay miles away in the Snowy mountains which gave Phryne the chance to take her beloved Gypsy Moth plane out for an adventure.

This is the fifth in the series of comic mysteries set in Australia during the Jazz Age featuring Phyrne Fisher. There is a strong overall story arc to this series so it would be best to read the series in order if at all possible. Those who are fans of the series on PBS need to be aware that the television series deviates markedly from the novels. Both series are good, and fans of one will probably enjoy the other despite the differences but do not jump into the middle of the book series because you have seen the television shows.

A common and notable comment I had read in a number of reviews was that there is a need for a floor mount. It appears the manufacture has now included a mount for both the top and bottom. Problem solved.

text:
I bought this to try out when I was trying the CGM and it was recommended on a CG site. It took a few washes for my hair to adapt to the change in product, and it made my hair fly away a bit. Worked really well on my hair. Soooo, even though it evaporated, I am going to give it one more try and see how it goes. A little concerned that the product left over after it evaporates is what is so good on my hair and won't get awesome results from the full product with my next purchase.

title: Quick Read
text:
This is an easy to read memoir that I sailed through, but it is also a book I’m not sure I needed to read. I received a paperback advance review copy. Not to sound harsh – but after finishing the book I wondered why this guy needed to write a memoir. There are no lessons learned, no real clue into much of his life other than what one could glean from the bio and book description.

We are quickly introduces to Jed Ringel, a soon-to-be-divorced, balding, short man with daughters. He was a successful lawyer turned IT business flipper. He apparently has plenty of cash. We see him devolve into alcohol-fueled living for a while, but he cleans his crap up so that made me happy for him. And I congratulate him on staying sober.

This dude has money to burn and he spends a good chunk on dating services, expensive dinners, overseas trips, and various address changes – all in the ultimate pursuit to find his ‘last great love.’ Some of the dates are comical and the book has humor sprinkled through, but overall this is a rich dude that doesn’t work that dates, sleeps with, and updates his dating bio to attract a broader range of gals. He ranges from picky to not picky, from dismissive, to moving to be near women that he does not know to see if things could work.

By the end of the book, you have read a moderate amount of failed dates in different countries and states. He appears to be a vacant father for the most part, a former alcoholic, and takes the reader to all the expensive restaurants. In the end, and this does not spoil the reader’s journey, he has some decent self-reflection, is still sober, and still has plenty of cash. I didn’t see much true transformation and at times it almost appeared Ringel was boasting about his sexual conquests and easy lifestyle.

So, some of the passages were humorous. I enjoyed one date that, to paraphrase – She showed up late and passed the table to say hi to friends, then came back and invited her friends to join them. Jed got up and left. Classic! I rooted for him on this one.

text:
Being an on and off fan of Casey Chaos's main band, Amen, i've heard, over the last 7 or 8 years, everything he's had to say on basically everything. people are (), there's barely anyone who truly cares for anything anymore, everyone's a whore, the cops sucks and so does government and mainstream music is worthless and devoured by mindless drones. that's just wonderful, for one album. but when your entire career is based on trying to prove, mostly to people who couldn't care less, how insanely punk rock you are, your whole schtick gets old quick.

the band consists of members, aside from Casey, from Emperor, Windir and Turbonegro. i loves me some emperor, windir ain't half bad, but turbonegro has never been my kind of thing. their gimmicks are boring and not really shocking. ("oh, look, we're fat and gay punk rockers" wonderful.)

the music is bland. there's really nothing more to say about it. if casey wasn't so devoted to proving himself all the time, i'm sure at least 4 of these songs could find their way onto some terrible 20th century fox action film. (hell, i happen to remember an Amen song being used on a Fox TV show by the name of Freaky Links, but i'm sure that was just the fault of the big scary evil record label.)

the lyrics are nothing new either. Casey's repeating old amen lyrics at some points, and everything else is just rehashed ranting on par with that of a 10th grade goth kid.

the sub-mediocrity of this album hurts because i know what an admirer of black metal Casey is, and you'd think with all the influences flowing into this band it would be a great chunk of harsh, venomous pissed off black metal. but it comes off more as a garage band who listen to nothing but Discharge and Turbonegro, and do a bad job of paying tribute.

pass it up if you get the chance.

Originality - 4

Production - 7

overall - 45% (and that's being generous)

title: be aware
text:
My 2004 audi A4 cabriolet was listed as compatible on their website, but the bottom two sponges pressed on the bumper so hard with 3 bikes (1 adult and 2 kids) that it cracked and permanently dented my plastic bumper cover. Hence, I am telling you now that the 2004 Audi A4 is NOT COMPATIBLE. in addition, the clips that go onto the side of the trunk was a V shape, say 10 degrees, but it was too small an angle so I could not easily close the trunk. the 10 degree angle was so narrow that the clip could not attach flush onto the trunk lid. as such, the only way that I could close the trunk was to slam it shut and accept the fact that my paint was going to get scuffed by the clip.

I am pretty sure that changing the design so that the 2 sponges that come into contact with the bumper are made wider, such as 1 foot wide total instead of the existing 2 x 2 inch wide sponges, it would put less weight per square inch. at the very least, it would likely not crack the plastic like it did for me.

If you have an all metal bumper, you should be fine, but a bumper with a plastic cover may be a problem.

if you can get a roof rack or tow hitch rack, you may be better off.

title: Not loud enough and not enough variety for sounds
text:
I bought this to use as an adhoc doorbell. I had been buying a different battery operated brand, but sourcing is scarce for that one now. I tried this Ecolink device out and was very disappointed. The device is huge compared to other Z-Wave devices, and the sounds that it makes are as loud as a cricket..that's it. It does have a volume adjustment, which is backwards from what you would assume (i.e. counter-clockwise increases volume). Even with the volume at maximum, You would never hear this chime if your TV was on. Given the size of the device, it should have a piezo siren inside to rival your home alarm. I tried the jumpers to switch between siren and chime...no significant difference.

There do not appear to be any Z-wave+ discoverable parameters to change the sounds. I have been pleased with other Ecolink Z-wave devices, but I have to strongly recommend against purchasing this one.

title: Value Spotting scope
text:
Used it to sight in rifles and spot elk. I've looked through many high end scopes, this falls short of those, but that's not the point. For 90 bucks you can get this thing and see what you need to see; bullet holes in a target easily out to 300 yards; elk points even farther.
Not as sharp near the edges, but I expected that for the price. Amazingly, the focus tuning is as good as I've ever used on a scope of almost any price. Housing is plastic but seems tough enough. Very light. I'm not sure how it would hold up if you dropped it on rock or something solid.
Eye piece cup folds down for eye-glass wearers, and stays down! I wish the tripod base was a bit more robust, but it works. The tripod itself is metal with baked-on no glare coating. It is very basic, but the legs seem pretty tough. But it has plastic axis components. Bag isn't anything to get excited about.
All in all, for under a 100 bucks, you get clear glass with fantastic focusing and smooth magnifying. I won't exaggerate the optics, but they are definitly worth the money, especially if you don't see the point in spending hundreds on a spotting scope.

I've had this mat for four months now, so I feel like I've had enough experience to write a review.

Initially the sticky side held the mat to my hardwood floor just fine. But, after a few weeks it started to lift up at the edges and dirt would stick to the mat. Little by little the mat would lift a little and dirt would stick. Now it's to the point where the entire bottom of the mat has dirt and hair and random debris. We are a pet free home and my wife is a clean freak, so our floors are very clean. It's just that any dirt that gets under the mat gets stuck.

I finally removed the mat today and the floor is covered with sticky stuff that I cannot get up. It's supposed to be water soluble, but it is not. I've been on my hands and knees scrubbing and it just won't relent and come up.

In short, don't get this mat. It actually traps dirt and it leaves a sticky residue on the floor.

title: heartbreaking
text:
alright so this book has the most beautiful cover ever. it also has trigger warnings (violence, sexual assault and rape) right next to the title page. what a beautiful example.
there's an author's note and it's at the start of the book and it creates the best atmosphere to start the story with? i was so grateful for this and that i could read it and have it diversify my reading and general life. that it's about a fantasy world that didn't come from a white place. that it's a celebration of all things that make this author.

about the book: IT HAS ASIAN F/F REP! also it's about a part that is often there in fantasy worlds but is hardly ever discussed: the king usually has many girls (either single different ones frequently, or many at the same time, or a group he cycles through, or ...)
here, he has eight, every year. they are of the lowest cast so should consider it an honour to be allowed in the court and spend time learning and the "priviledge" of being with the heavenly master. so they're slaves. and they're picked specifically for him to have sex with. and it's horrible.
and yet the book is strong and feminist talks about this important topic with nuance.

Her kisses heal the part of me that the King broke. They tell me: You are strong, Lei. You are beautiful. And, always, most important, you are yours.

it's about the power in you and the impact of things. it's about rape and power and violence and how people want power and use it in every way to get more/create fear/get what they want and all the dangers about this.
it's also about love, and reclaiming yourself. i love the trope subversion, almost, that this wasn't a tormented king the main character fell in love with, but another girl. about being strong and fighting in the ways you can. about surviving. warriors and survivors and victims and a culture that lets things happen.

there are so many things that need to be said about this and this book is doing great. it also has an unapologetic asian-inspired world. i don't think the books flow was as smooth in all places (plot? pacing? i don't know what it was, but something) but damn if it's not incredibly worth reading
(also important: a reminder that it's okay to not be able to read books like this if they are too triggering or won't be healthy for you. this does not define your worth.)

please do note it has a very fatphobic moment on pgs 32/33 in which the only character that is ever described as fat is also described as ugly and is prejudiced and wrong (see: your only fat character is a villain). this was incredibly unnecessary and was never addressed again.
also: the girl are chosen mainly based on youth and beauty so what society sees as beautiful plays a big role in the book

cw: rape, attempted rape, sexual assault/abuse, violence, death, loss of a loved one, trying to destroy an entire group of people, abduction, unchallenged fatphobic remark, talk about infertility, mentions of a pregnancy preventing drink

The top eye shadow palette is a very nice palette with lots of red and orange tones. You also get some neutral brown / beige tones in it for transition shades. You have 11 mattes which are great for your base eye shadow and then 4 shimmers to liven it up. Then there is one heavy glitter that I wouldn’t put around my eyes but I know some people do, totally up to you but I would be careful. It is very pretty though.

Then you swivel that palette out of the way to get to the next one, the blue one. In this one you get a very nice all white and a total of 9 mattes. Then you get 6 shimmers and again a gllitter that I would not put near my eyes but it is very pretty. In the colors they are mostly blue but you are also getting 3 in the brown scheme and one of the shimmers is a grayish-purple that is very nice.

Next is the purple palette. In this one you have 11 mattes, 4 shimmers and again one of those glitters that are stunning but not for the eyes in my opinion. This one has a stunning copper shimmer that is gorgeous and in my eyes the most stunning palette.

Last is the yellow and green palette. In this one you get 11 mattes, 4 shimmers including a stunning white one, and the typical glitter that is not for the eyes for me at least.

I have to say you get a stunning array of colors in mattes and shimmers. The glitters I am not a fan of because they are just so coarse and in my eyes is just asking for trouble near the eyes. I can just see them getting into my eyes and causing issues so for me these are more for maybe on the cheeks or the body applications or not at all really but others can do as they choose. They are stunning in regards to color though I give them that.

The mix of mattes and shimmers is great since I prefer having more mattes to get a good eye shadow makeup going and then highlight it with the right shimmers. Their shimmers are fantastic and best applied with the finger I found. The eye shadows overall are not the most pigmented and it takes a bit to build them up but you can get some really nice looks with them. They are easy to work with overall so no issue there.

What I wish it had, yes it is nice they threw in some brown neutral tone for transitions, but I wish they had either a palette with just brown towns and added another $5 to the price or just added a couple more brown tones. I am also surprised they don’t have a black in there to be honest. They did add a couple of gold-bronze-copper kind of colors but if they would have just added one more palette with browns then they could have eliminated those transition tones from each of the color palettes so given them more colors there and then added some nice brown tones overall (16 more). That and the lack of pigmentation are my only complaints but other than that for the price this is really a great purchase.

Overall I have to say that this is a good step in the Muppet franchise because it brings Kermit, Fozziem Gonzo, et al to a whole new generation and it would be good to see it started up again.

text:
As one other reviewer noted, there is a growing trend of series-type books leaving off on a cliffhanger, especially when they are offered for free. I understand the frustration of getting right into a story and then being left wanting more, but that really is the point. You got the first part for free so that you could get a feel for the author's writing, the overall level of quality to the book (something that is lacking in many paid-for ebooks these days), and is then encouraged to purchase more books by the author. Saul Tanpepper's books are all priced extremely reasonably and he deserved to be paid for the work that goes into writing. As an author myself, I know that sometimes the writing process can feel like you're pulling out your own teeth.

This first instalment of the Gameland series really caught my attention because it has a refreshing take on the zombie experience. I'm not going to summarize the plot line, since you can read the book teaser to get a good idea of how things go. As a geek, I really appreciate Tanpepper's technological references. title: An Acceptable But (Somewhat) Bare-Bones Theory Book
text:
Given all of the recent excitement around the topics of clean/renewable energy, energy conservation and efficiency and the embryonic re-birth of (high-tech) manufacturing in the developed, industrialized world, Professor Kitai's book on PV and LED theory really is timely.

This book has a number of merits. In six detailed chapters, the book covers all of the mainstream theory behind PV and LED applications from the standpoint of the semiconductor quite adequately. Each of the six chapters making up the book (plus three appendices covering physical constants, semiconductor properties and supporting theory) is very well organized and arguably could be seen as booklets in and of themselves. I especially liked how each chapter was organized, first with an overview of the objectives of the chapter and a general introduction giving the plan of the chapter, a chapter summary, four to six brief suggestions for further reading related to the chapter topics and about a couple of dozen problems (unfortunately, without solutions). Most of the reading suggestions are fairly recent publications in the field, pretty much guaranteeing that students get exposed to very latest advances in the field. While the book contains a good helping of Greek, integrals and derivatives, one can tell that the author took great pains to economize on the use of formulae, thus ensuring that only absolute necessary mathematics are presented to bring about understanding of the topics.

However, the book also has a few minor demerits. First, there are no solutions to the problems presented at the end of the chapter, and within the chapter, there is a paucity of worked problems. The good professor can mostly be forgiven for this one given that most of the end-of-chapter problems are more qualitative, encouraging the student/reader to seek out additional information on the web or sketch out solutions. Second, while the author did write in the active voice (which in itself is a great relief when reading any theoretical physics book- trust me), the writing was a bit stilted and very repetitive, with the author beginning, it seemed, just about every other sentence with the word `Consider...". Third, although the textbook comes replete with oodles of graphs, diagrams and charts, all in black and white, the book generally lacks color, making it a bit bland. Fourth, and admittedly a very minor demerit, the book is soft-cover- a definite no-no for a serious theoretical text like this one, which, by the way, is quite accessible (I am not a physical sciences major, but even I, given my admittedly poor grades in upper division engineering coursework, could follow the narrative). Finally, I did find a major and glaring omission within the book: Table 3.1 on luminescence types on Page 124 is missing a key entry- that on bioluminescence (and yes, saying that bioluminescence is a chemical process as opposed to a physical one and thus OK to neglect in a text detailing the semi-conductor basis for PV and LED applications is, frankly, a bit of a dodge).

Overall, this textbook is long on theory, but light on application. Although it contains lots of graphs, charts and diagrams, it has no cool pictures of the actual devices whose function revolves around the underlying theory presented in the book. Granted, there's one black and white pic/graphic of an odd-looking LED device on page 246, but that's about it. This is a bit of a let-down, as it's the really cool PV and LED devices that generate the interest in the subject, and it would have been nice if the reader could, at least on occasion, go ooh-and-aah over them. Here, I am thinking specifically about some of the more conceptual designs as well as the blandly commercial ones that resulted from the efforts such as those of the US Department of Energy/Sandia Labs LED lighting challenge, the ongoing work of the Center for LED lighting at Rochester Institute of Technology or some of the work being undertaken in the private sector by the likes of GE, Phillips and Siemens.

Still, the book does live up to its intended purpose as a suitable introductory textbook on the topic for upper-level undergraduate students, and future editions of this book should endeavor to add a little color and perhaps get some collaboration, in the form of submissions of cool pictures and diagrams of PV and LED devices (in color please) from a few of the leading private sector and academic groups working in the field. In sum, the author gets kudos for publishing a very well organized and accessible theoretical book on a hot- and growing hotter- topic.

text:
This was my first purchase of a door closer and I needed it for the internal door to the garage which kept banging closed. The instructions are terrible to say the least, so google Marie door closer and you will see plenty of videos. Once you see the video it all becomes clear and I installed in 5 mins. You can control the door closing speed & the latch with a screwdriver, but use small turns & test, repeat if necessary.
Good product for the price and I would recommend it to anybody who needs to stop a door banging closed.
